hindi: अब इसके बाद हम विधिशोणितीय अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on blood and regimen (Vidhiśoṇitīya).
notes: The chapter name Vidhiśoṇitīya is a derived title word and is not split; it takes up vidhinā śoṇitam of unit 3.

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा।
english: Thus said the venerable Ātreya.

words.gloss: of place, time and habitual suitability
words.gram: n. gen. pl., dvandva (okas-sātmya = habitual suitability)
m. nom. sg., ppp. caus. sam-pra-√kāś

hindi: देहधारियों का रक्त विधि से उत्पन्न होने पर शुद्ध होता है, वह विधि जो देश, काल और ओकसात्म्य के विषय में बताई गई है।
english: In embodied beings, blood produced by following the regimen (vidhi) is pure, the regimen of place, time and habitual suitability (okasātmya) that has been set forth.
notes: okasātmya (printed kāla + okas giving kālaukas) = habitual suitability, the okaḥsātmya of the glossary. The relative clause defines which vidhi is meant; the text does not say here where it was set forth. deśa-kāla-okas-sātmyānām may also be read as 'of what is suitable (sātmya) to place, time and habit (okas)', sātmya governing all three.
lines_deva: विधिना शोणितं जातं शुद्धं भवति देहिनाम्
lines_iast: vidhinā śoṇitaṃ jātaṃ śuddhaṃ bhavati dehinām

words.gloss: with strength, complexion, happiness and life-span

hindi: क्योंकि वह शुद्ध रक्त प्राणियों को बल, वर्ण, सुख और आयु से युक्त करता है; क्योंकि (जीवन) रक्त का अनुसरण करता है।
english: For that pure blood endows living beings with strength, complexion, happiness and life-span; for (life) follows the blood.
notes: The second half-line is two syllables short and anuvartate (3 sg.) lacks a subject; '(life)' in the translations is supplied from āyuṣā of the first line and is only a stopgap. prāṇinaḥ is taken as acc. pl. object of yunakti. The 14-syllable half-line is recorded here only; no correction can be shown from the chunk, so there is no text_flag.

words.gloss: spoiled, (taken) in excess, sharp and hot

words.gram: m. inst. pl., dvandva with ati-

hindi: बिगड़े हुए, अधिक मात्रा वाले, तीक्ष्ण और उष्ण मद्यों से और उसी प्रकार के अन्य (पेयों) से; उसी तरह अति लवण और क्षार से, अम्ल से और कटु पदार्थों से भी;
english: By wines that are spoiled, (taken) in excess, sharp and hot, and by other (drinks) of that kind; likewise by excess of salt and alkalis (kṣāra), by sour things and by pungent things too;

text_flags.why: vidhra is not a word; tad-vidha 'of that kind' (inst. pl. tadvidhaiḥ) fits the grammar and sense, agreeing with anyaiḥ; the extra r adds no syllable

notes: The sentence (list of causes) runs on through unit 10, where the verb śoṇitaṃ saṃpraduṣyati comes. bahu is taken as 'in excess'; it could also mean simply 'much, abundant'. ati- is taken to govern both lavaṇa and kṣāra.

words.gloss: by use of kulattha, māṣa, niṣpāva and sesame oil
words.gram: n. inst. pl., tat-puruṣa with inner dvandva

words.gloss: of piṇḍālu, mūlaka and the like

hindi: कुलत्थ, माष, निष्पाव और तिल के तेल के सेवन से; पिण्डालु, मूलक आदि सब प्रकार के हरे शाकों के (सेवन से),
english: by the use of kulattha, māṣa, niṣpāva and sesame oil; by (the use) of piṇḍālu, mūlaka and other green vegetables of all kinds,
notes: The genitives of line 2 depend on sevanāt in unit 7. Identifications: kulattha = horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum (standard); māṣa = black gram, Vigna mungo (standard); niṣpāva = Lablab purpureus (probable); piṇḍālu = a yam, Dioscorea sp. (disputed); mūlaka = radish, Raphanus sativus (standard). sarvaśaḥ could also mean 'in every way, entirely'.

words.gloss: of the prasaha (animals that seize by force)
of curd, sour things, whey and śukta

hindi: जलज, आनूप और बिलवासी प्राणियों के तथा प्रसह प्राणियों के (मांस के) सेवन से; दही, अम्ल पदार्थ, मस्तु और शुक्त के तथा सुरा और सौवीरक के (सेवन से);
english: from the use (of the flesh) of water-born, marsh and burrow-dwelling animals and of the prasaha (animals that seize by force); (from the use) of curd, sour things, whey (mastu) and śukta, and of surā and sauvīraka;

text_flags.why: possible: sukta gives no sense in a list of curd preparations and sour drinks; śukta (a fermented sour preparation) fits; s for ś changes no syllable

notes: 'Flesh' is understood: the text names only the animal groups. baila (from bila 'burrow') = burrow-dwellers. amla is taken as a separate member 'sour things'; it could also qualify mastu ('sour whey'). surā, sauvīraka and śukta are kept in Sanskrit.

words.gram: m. gen. pl., pres. part. pra-√svap

hindi: विरुद्ध, सड़े-गले और दुर्गन्धित पदार्थों के भक्षण से; और द्रव, स्निग्ध और गुरु पदार्थ खाकर दिन में सोने वालों का;
english: by eating incompatible, decomposed and putrid things; and of those who sleep by day after eating liquid, unctuous and heavy things;
notes: upaklinna literally 'moistened through, soaked', here taken as decomposed. The genitive prasvapatām ('of those who...') continues in unit 9 (bhajatām) and goes with śoṇitaṃ saṃpraduṣyati of unit 10 ('the blood of those who ...').

words.gloss: of those who eat to excess
from suppression of the urge to vomit

hindi: अधिक खाने वालों का, उसी प्रकार क्रोध और धूप तथा अग्नि का सेवन करने वालों का; छर्दि के वेग को रोकने से, और समय पर रक्त न निकालने से;
english: of those who eat to excess, and likewise of those who resort to anger, and to the sun and fire; from suppressing the urge to vomit, and from not letting blood at the (proper) time;
notes: atyādānām is read as gen. pl. of atyāda 'one who eats to excess' (ati-ā-√ad), parallel to prasvapatām (unit 8) and bhajatām; the printed text needs no change. These genitives go with śoṇitaṃ saṃpraduṣyati of unit 10. avasecana = letting out of blood; anavasecana is its absence.

words.gloss: by indigestion and eating on top of undigested food
from the nature of the Śarad season

hindi: श्रम, अभिघात और संताप से, उसी प्रकार अजीर्ण और अध्यशन से, और शरद् काल के स्वभाव से रक्त दूषित हो जाता है।
english: By fatigue, injury and heat, likewise by indigestion (ajīrṇa) and eating on top of undigested food (adhyaśana), and from the nature of the Śarad season, the blood becomes vitiated.
notes: This verb closes the list of causes begun in unit 5. saṃtāpa taken as heat (exposure, burning); it could also mean distress. Śarad is roughly autumn (season equivalent).

words.gloss: putrid odour of nose and mouth

hindi: तब रक्त से उत्पन्न अनेक प्रकार के रोग उत्पन्न होते हैं: मुखपाक, आँखों की लालिमा, नाक और मुख की सड़ी गन्ध,
english: Then diseases born of blood, of various kinds, arise: mukhapāka (inflammation of the mouth), redness of the eyes, putrid odour of the nose and mouth,
notes: The list of blood-born diseases runs through unit 16. pāka literally 'cooking, ripening', i.e. inflammation or suppuration.

words.gloss: gulma, upakuśa, vīsarpa, raktapitta and pramīlaka

hindi: गुल्म, उपकुश, वीसर्प, रक्तपित्त, प्रमीलक, विद्रधि, रक्तमेह, प्रदर, वातशोणित,
english: gulma, upakuśa, vīsarpa, raktapitta, pramīlaka, vidradhi (abscess), raktameha, pradara, vātaśoṇita,
notes: Disease names kept in Sanskrit with no identifications. upakuśa and pramīlaka are given no gloss beyond the name.

words.gram: f. nom. sg., abstract of bahuvrīhi

hindi: विवर्णता, अग्नि की मन्दता, प्यास, शरीर का भारीपन, संताप, अति दुर्बलता, अरुचि और सिर का दर्द,
english: discoloration, weakness of the digestive fire (agni), thirst, heaviness of the body, burning heat, extreme weakness, loss of taste (aruci) and pain in the head,

words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with inner dvandva
f. nom. sg., abstract of bahuvrīhi

hindi: अन्न-पान का विदाह, तिक्त और अम्ल उद्गार, क्लम, क्रोध की अधिकता, बुद्धि का संमोह, मुख का खारापन,
english: burning (vidāha) of food and drink, bitter and sour belching, exhaustion (klama), abundance of anger, confusion of the intellect, saltiness in the mouth,
notes: buddheḥ is taken with saṃmohaḥ ('confusion of the intellect'); it could also be read with krodhapracuratā ('the intellect's abundance of anger'). vidāha of food = burning during digestion.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with inner dvandva

hindi: स्वेद, शरीर की दुर्गन्ध, मद, कम्प, स्वर का क्षय, तन्द्रा और निद्रा की अधिकता, और अन्धकार का अधिक दिखना,
english: sweating, foul smell of the body, intoxication (mada), tremor, loss of voice, excess of drowsiness and sleep, and excessive seeing of darkness,
notes: daurgandhya (dur- 'bad' + gandha) is printed, hence 'foul smell'. tamaso 'tidarśanam: seeing darkness in excess; literal rendering kept.

words.gloss: itching, arus, koṭha, eruptions, kuṣṭha, carmadala and the like
words.gram: m. nom. pl., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

hindi: कण्डू, अरुः, कोठ, पिडका, कुष्ठ, चर्मदल आदि; ये सभी विकार रक्त पर आश्रित जानने चाहिए।
english: itching (kaṇḍū), arus, koṭha, eruptions (piḍakā), kuṣṭha, carmadala and the like: all these disorders are to be known as based on blood.
notes: arus (in compound aruḥ), koṭha, kuṣṭha and carmadala kept in Sanskrit; literal sense of arus 'sore', of carmadala 'splitting of the skin'. sarva (printed) is sarve with the e dropped before eva in sandhi, as is regular.

words.gloss: with cold, hot, unctuous, dry and other (measures)
words.gram: n. inst. pl., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

hindi: जो रोग साध्य हों और शीत, उष्ण, स्निग्ध, रूक्ष आदि उपायों से ठीक प्रकार चिकित्सित किए जाने पर सिद्ध न हों, उन्हें रक्तज समझना चाहिए।
english: Those diseases which, though curable and properly treated with cold, hot, unctuous, dry and other (measures), are not cured, one should recognise as born of blood.
notes: samyak is taken with upakrāntāḥ ('properly treated'); it could also go with sādhyāḥ ('fully curable'). The ca after upakrāntāḥ is read as concessive ('though').
lines_deva: सम्यक् साध्या न सिध्यन्ति रक्तजांस्तान् विभावयेत्
lines_iast: samyak sādhyā na sidhyanti raktajāṃstān vibhāvayet

hindi: रक्त के रोगों में रक्तपित्त को दूर करने वाली चिकित्सा करनी चाहिए, तथा विरेक, उपवास और रक्त का स्रावण।
english: In diseases of the blood one should carry out the treatment that removes raktapitta, and purgation, fasting and letting out of blood.

words.gloss: according to the measure of strength and doṣa
words.gram: n. abl. sg., tat-puruṣa with inner dvandva

hindi: बल और दोष के प्रमाण के अनुसार, या रक्त की शुद्धि (के आधार) से, या आशय को भली भाँति देखकर, मनुष्य का रक्त निकालना चाहिए।
english: One should let out the person's blood either according to the measure of strength and doṣa, or by (the standard of) the purity of the blood, or having carefully examined the āśaya (site).
notes: viśuddhyā rudhirasya (instrumental) is rendered 'by (the standard of) the purity of the blood'; it may mean letting blood until it flows pure, but the text gives only the instrumental. āśaya kept in Sanskrit ('site, reservoir'); the text does not say which site is meant.

hindi: वात से (दूषित रक्त) अरुण आभा वाला, विशद, झागदार और पतला होता है; पित्त से रक्त पीला और काला होता है और उष्णता के कारण देर से जमता है।
english: (Blood vitiated) by Vāta is reddish in appearance, non-slimy, frothy and thin; by Pitta the blood is yellow and dark and, because of heat, clots slowly.
notes: duṣṭam of unit 21 ('vitiated') is understood here. pītāsita can be read 'yellow and dark' or 'yellowish-dark'.

words.gloss: with the signs of all three

hindi: कफ से दूषित (रक्त) थोड़ा पाण्डु, पिच्छिल, तन्तुयुक्त और घन होता है; संसर्ग से मिले-जुले लक्षणों वाला, और सान्निपातिक तीनों के लक्षणों वाला होता है।
english: Vitiated by Kapha, it is slightly pale, slimy, stringy and compact; from a combination (of two doṣas) it has combined signs, and from all three together (sānnipātika) it has the signs of all three.
notes: tantumat literally 'having threads'. saṃsarga is taken as the combination of two doṣas, contrasted with sānnipātika (all three); the text does not say 'two'.

words.gloss: with the lustre of gold and of the indragopa
words.gram: n. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva
n. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

words.gloss: of the colour of the guñjā fruit

hindi: तपाए हुए सोने और इन्द्रगोप की आभा वाले, कमल और अलक्तक के समान, और गुञ्जा फल के समान रंग वाले रक्त को शुद्ध जानो।
english: Know as pure the blood that has the lustre of refined gold (tapanīya) and of the indragopa, that resembles the lotus and lac-dye (alaktaka), and that has the colour of the guñjā fruit.
notes: tapanīya = gold (literally 'to be heated', i.e. refined gold). indragopa kept in Sanskrit (a creature; no identification). Identification: guñjā = Abrus precatorius (standard).

words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva (adjectival) with ati-

hindi: रक्त निकाल दिए जाने पर ऐसा अन्न-पान हितकर है जो न अधिक उष्ण हो न अधिक शीतल, लघु और दीपन हो; क्योंकि तब शरीर अस्थिर रक्त वाला होता है, और अग्नि की विशेष रूप से रक्षा करनी चाहिए।
english: When the blood has been let out, food and drink that is neither too hot nor too cold, light and stimulating to digestion is beneficial; for then the body has unsteady blood, and the digestive fire (agni) is to be protected especially.

text_flags.why: anavastita is not a word; anavasthita 'unsteady' (an-ava-√sthā) fits the grammar and sense of a body whose blood has just been let out; t for th changes no syllable

notes: Upajāti verse (11 syllables a quarter). anavasthitāsṛk is read as a bahuvrīhi agreeing with śarīram ('having unsteady blood').

words.gloss: whose complexion and senses are clear
words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

words.gloss: whose digester and urges are unobstructed
words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva
m. acc. sg., tat-puruṣa with inner dvandva

hindi: जिसका वर्ण और इन्द्रियाँ प्रसन्न हों, जो इन्द्रियों के विषयों की इच्छा करता हो, जिसका पचाने वाला और जिसके वेग बिना बाधा के हों, जो सुख से युक्त, तुष्टि और बल से सम्पन्न हो, ऐसे पुरुष को शुद्ध रक्त वाला कहते हैं।
english: The man whose complexion and senses are clear, who desires the objects of the senses, whose digester (paktṛ) and urges are unobstructed, who is endowed with happiness and possessed of contentment and strength, him they call a man of pure blood.

text_flags.why: metre: in this upajāti quarter the 9th syllable must be light; va-dan-ti fits, van-dan-ti makes it heavy (the other three quarters scan correctly); sense: a statement of signs, cf. viddhi 'know' in unit 22

notes: Upajāti verse. '(puṣṭi-)' is printed in round brackets after tuṣṭibalopapannaṃ, apparently as an alternative reading puṣṭi- 'nourishment' for tuṣṭi- 'contentment'; the input does not say what the brackets mean, it is not counted in the metre, and it is not applied. paktṛ (the digester) is read with vega as a dvandva ('digester and urges'); it could also be read as a tat-puruṣa 'the force of the digester'. vadanti (metre) is used in the split and translation; src keeps vandanti.

words.gram: n. acc. pl., upapada tat-puruṣa with inner dvandva

hindi: किन्तु जब कुपित मल, अलग-अलग या सब मिलकर, रक्त को वहन करने वाले और रस तथा संज्ञा को वहन करने वाले स्रोतों को
english: But when the aggravated malas, singly or all together, the channels that carry blood and those that carry rasa and consciousness (saṃjñā),
notes: The sentence continues into unit 26 (pratihatya avatiṣṭhante 'having obstructed, settle'). malāḥ (glossary: waste) are here said to be aggravated (kupita); units 28 and 29 name vāyu, Pitta and Kapha as the agents, so the malas here are probably the doṣas. rasa is kept in Sanskrit (here the bodily fluid, not taste).
lines_deva: पृथक् पृथक् समस्ता वा स्रोतांसि कुपिता मलाः
lines_iast: pṛthak pṛthak samastā vā srotāṃsi kupitā malāḥ

words.gloss: of one habituated to unclean food
whose self is covered by rajas and delusion
words.gram: m. gen. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

hindi: मलिन आहार के अभ्यस्त और रज तथा मोह से आवृत आत्मा वाले मनुष्य के, रोककर ठहर जाते हैं, तब रोग उत्पन्न होते हैं:
english: of a person habituated to unclean food, whose self is covered by rajas and delusion (moha), having obstructed (them), settle (there), then diseases arise:
notes: Continues the sentence of unit 25; the diseases are named in unit 27. rajas kept in Sanskrit (the quality of the mind).

hindi: मद, मूर्च्छा और संन्यास। विचक्षण व्यक्ति इनके हेतु, लक्षण और उपशान्ति में उत्तरोत्तर बल की अधिकता जाने।
english: mada (intoxication), mūrcchāya (fainting) and saṃnyāsa (collapse). The discerning one should know that among these the strength increases successively in cause, signs and alleviation.
notes: mada, mūrcchāya and saṃnyāsa are kept in Sanskrit with literal glosses (saṃnyāsa literally 'laying down, abandonment'); no modern identifications. mūrcchāya is kept as printed (the masculine noun of the same root as mūrcchā). 'Strength' increases in the order given: saṃnyāsa is the strongest.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., pres. part. caus. vi-√kṣubh

hindi: जब वायु चित्त के दुर्बल स्थान में प्रवेश करता है, तब वह मनुष्य के मन को क्षुब्ध करता हुआ उसकी संज्ञा को मोहित कर देता है।
english: When Vāta (vāyu) enters the weakened seat of the mind, then, agitating the mind, it confuses the person's consciousness.
notes: jantoḥ may go with manaḥ or with saṃjñām ('the person's mind / consciousness'); the sense is the same.
lines_deva: दुर्बलं चेतसः स्थानं यदा वायुः प्रपद्यते
lines_iast: durbalaṃ cetasaḥ sthānaṃ yadā vāyuḥ prapadyate

words.gram: m. nom. sg., pres. part. caus. vi-√kṣubh

hindi: इसी प्रकार पित्त और इसी प्रकार कफ मनुष्यों के मन को क्षुब्ध करता हुआ संज्ञा को व्याकुलता में पहुँचा देता है; और इसमें जो भेद है वह बताया जाएगा।
english: In the same way Pitta, and likewise Kapha, agitating the mind of men, brings consciousness into confusion; and the distinction here will be stated.
notes: vikṣobhayan and nayati are singular, applying to Pitta and Kapha each in turn. The distinction is given from unit 30 on.

words.gloss: whose speech is halting, profuse and hurried
words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

words.gloss: whose movements are unsteady and stumbling
words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

words.gloss: whose appearance is dry, dusky and reddish
words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

hindi: जिसकी वाणी अटकती हुई, अधिक और तेज़ हो, जिसकी चेष्टाएँ चंचल और लड़खड़ाती हुई हों, और जिसकी आकृति रूक्ष, श्याव और अरुण हो, उसे वात के मद से ग्रस्त जानना चाहिए।
english: One whose speech is halting, profuse and hurried, whose movements are unsteady and stumbling, and whose appearance is dry, dusky and reddish, one should know to be seized by the mada of Vāta.
notes: sakta literally 'stuck, clinging', taken as halting speech. śyāva = dusky, dark-brownish.

words.gloss: whose speech is angry and harsh

words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

words.gloss: whose appearance is red, yellow or dark
words.gram: m. acc. sg., bahuvrīhi with inner dvandva

hindi: जिसकी वाणी क्रोधयुक्त और कठोर हो, जिसे मार-पीट और कलह प्रिय हो, और जिसकी आकृति लाल, पीली या काली हो, उसे पित्त के मद से ग्रस्त जानना चाहिए।
english: One whose speech is angry and harsh, who is fond of fighting and quarrels, and whose appearance is red, yellow or dark, one should know to be seized by the mada of Pitta.
notes: raktapītāsita may be 'red, yellow and dark' together or as alternatives; 'or' is used in the translation.

words.gloss: whose speech is scanty and incoherent

hindi: जिसकी वाणी बहुत थोड़ी और असम्बद्ध हो, जो तन्द्रा और आलस्य से युक्त हो, पाण्डु वर्ण का हो और गहरे चिन्तन में लीन रहे, उसे कफ-मद से ग्रस्त जानना चाहिए।
english: One whose speech is scanty and incoherent, who is given to drowsiness and sloth, pale, and intent on brooding, should be known as possessed by the mada (intoxication) of Kapha.
notes: svalpa is analysed as su-alpa 'very little'. pāṇḍu is taken as the adjective 'pale', not the disease name.

hindi: सन्निपात से उत्पन्न मद में ये सभी रूप होते हैं। मद्य के मद जैसा रूप रखने वाला मद शीघ्र उत्पन्न होता है और शीघ्र शान्त हो जाता है।
english: In mada caused by sannipāta (all three doṣas combined) all these forms [appear]. Mada that has the appearance of liquor-mada arises and subsides quickly.
notes: The first line has no verb; 'appear' is understood. kṣipram is taken with both jāyate and śāmyati. The second half may also be read as a property of the sannipāta intoxication itself.

words.gloss: the triad of Vāta, Pitta and Kapha

hindi: जो मद्य से उत्पन्न कहा गया है, जो विष से उत्पन्न है और जो रक्त से उत्पन्न है, ये सभी मद वात, पित्त और कफ इन तीनों के बिना नहीं होते।
english: That which is declared to be caused by liquor, that born of poison and that which arises from blood: all these madas do not occur without the triad of Vāta, Pitta and Kapha.
notes: raudhira is a derivative of rudhira 'blood'.
lines_deva: यश्च मद्यकृतः प्रोक्तो विषजो रौधिरश्च यः
lines_iast: yaśca madyakṛtaḥ prokto viṣajo raudhiraśca yaḥ

hindi: आकाश को नीला या काला अथवा लाल देखता हुआ वह अन्धकार में प्रवेश करता है और जल्दी होश में आ जाता है।
english: Seeing the sky blue or black or red, he enters darkness and comes to again quickly.
notes: The subject (the one who faints) is understood; unit 36 names this as the Vāta type of fainting (mūrcchāya). yadi vā is the disjunctive 'or'. athavāruṇam is read athavā aruṇam 'or red'.

hindi: वात से उत्पन्न मूर्च्छा में कम्पन, अंगमर्द, हृदय में तीव्र पीड़ा, कृशता और धूसर-लाल छाया होती है।
english: In mūrcchāya (fainting) arising from Vāta there are trembling, body-ache, severe pain of the heart, emaciation and a dusky-reddish complexion.
notes: cchāyā: the ch is doubled after the preceding vowel (śyāvāruṇā cchāyā), a normal spelling; the word is chāyā. mūrcchāya (m.) is the word this chapter uses for fainting.

hindi: आकाश को लाल या हरे रंग का अथवा पीला देखता हुआ वह अन्धकार में प्रवेश करता है और पसीने से युक्त होकर होश में आता है।
english: Seeing the sky red or green-coloured or else yellow, he enters darkness and comes to again sweating.
notes: atha api vā together mean 'or else'. Unit 38 names this as the Pitta type of fainting.
lines_deva: रक्तं हरितवर्णं वा वियत् पीतमथापि वा
lines_iast: raktaṃ haritavarṇaṃ vā viyat pītamathāpi vā

hindi: पित्त से उत्पन्न मूर्च्छा में रोगी प्यास और सन्ताप से युक्त होता है, उसकी आँखें लाल, पीली और व्याकुल होती हैं, मल पतला हो जाता है और वह पीली आभा वाला होता है।
english: In mūrcchāya arising from Pitta, he is thirsty and burning with heat, his eyes are red, yellow and unsteady, his stools are loose, and he looks yellowish.
notes: saṃbhinna-varcas: literally 'whose faeces are broken up', i.e. loose stools. ākula 'agitated, unsteady' is taken with the eyes.

hindi: आकाश को बादल जैसा अथवा अन्धकार के घने समूहों से ढका हुआ देखता हुआ वह अन्धकार में प्रवेश करता है और देर से होश में आता है।
english: Seeing the sky like a cloud, or covered by masses of darkness, he enters darkness and comes to again after a long time.
notes: tamoghana may also mean 'dark clouds'. Unit 40 names this as the Kapha type of fainting.

hindi: कफ से उत्पन्न मूर्च्छा में रोगी के अंग भारी होते हैं, मानो गीले चमड़े से ही ढके हों, और वह मुँह में पानी आने तथा मिचली से युक्त होता है।
english: In mūrcchāya arising from Kapha, he has heavy limbs, covered just as if by a wet hide, and he has watering of the mouth and nausea.
notes: praseka is taken as watering of the mouth (flow of saliva); it may mean any discharge. The instrumentals describe the patient: 'with heavy limbs as though wrapped in a wet hide'.

hindi: सन्निपात से उत्पन्न मूर्च्छा सभी लक्षणों वाली होती है और अपस्मार की तरह आती है; वह प्राणी को शीघ्र गिरा देती है, किन्तु वीभत्स चेष्टाओं के बिना।
english: [Mūrcchāya] from sannipāta has all the features and comes on like apasmāra; it fells the person quickly, but without the loathsome movements.
notes: The subject (the fainting from sannipāta) is understood from units 36 to 40; sa is masculine, agreeing with mūrcchāya. apasmāra kept as the Sanskrit disease name. 'but' is supplied to render vinā's contrast with apasmāra.

hindi: जब देहधारियों के दोष अपना वेग पूरा कर लेते हैं, तब मद और मूर्च्छा स्वयं ही शान्त हो जाते हैं; किन्तु संन्यास औषधियों के बिना शान्त नहीं होता।
english: When the doṣas of embodied beings have run their course, mada and mūrcchāya subside indeed by themselves; saṃnyāsa (collapse) does not [subside] without medicines.
notes: Locative absolute: doṣeṣu kṛtavegeṣu. vega of a disease = course. saṃnyāsa here is the disorder named in this chapter (a collapse), not renunciation; the verb 'subside' is carried over to it.

words.gloss: lodged in the seats of life

hindi: अत्यन्त बलवान मल प्राणों के आयतनों में आश्रित होकर, वाणी, शरीर और मन की चेष्टा को छीनकर, दुर्बल प्राणी को संन्यास में गिरा देते हैं।
english: The very strong malas, lodged in the seats of life (prāṇa), seize the activity of speech, body and mind and cast the weak person down [into saṃnyāsa].
notes: malāḥ (rendered 'malas', waste) here are the vitiating agents; unit 42 speaks of the doṣas in the same context. saṃnyasyanti is the verb from which saṃnyāsa 'collapse' is formed. ākṣipya may also mean 'having struck down, having taken away'.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa; ppp. saṃ-ni-√as

hindi: संन्यास से गिराया गया वह मनुष्य लकड़ी जैसा जड़ और मृत के समान हो जाता है; तुरन्त फल देने वाली चिकित्सा-क्रियाओं को छोड़कर, वह शीघ्र प्राणों से वियुक्त हो जाता है।
english: That man, cast down by saṃnyāsa, become like a log and resembling the dead, is quickly parted from life, except [through] treatments that bear immediate fruit.
notes: muktvā 'leaving aside' is used in the sense 'except': without immediately effective treatment he soon dies. kāṣṭhībhūta is a cvi formation 'become wood'.

hindi: जैसे बुद्धिमान मनुष्य गहरे जल में डूबते हुए पात्र को तल तक पहुँचने से पहले शीघ्रता से पकड़ लेता है, वैसे ही संन्यास से पीड़ित को पकड़ना चाहिए।
english: As a wise man would quickly seize a vessel sinking in deep water before it has reached the bottom, so [should one seize] one afflicted by saṃnyāsa.
notes: The verb gṛhṇīyāt is carried into the second clause. durga 'hard to pass' is rendered 'deep'.

hindi: अञ्जन, अवपीड, धूम और प्रधमन, सुइयों से चुभोना, दाह और नाखूनों के बीच दबाना प्रशस्त है।
english: Collyria (añjana), pressed-juice nasal drops (avapīḍa), medicated smokings, insufflations (pradhamana), pricking with needles, burning, and pressing between the nails are approved.
notes: The list continues into unit 47, whose hitaṃ tasyāvabodhane 'beneficial for rousing him' applies to these too. pradhamana: blowing a powder into the nose. nakhāntare 'between (under) the nails'.

hindi: सिर के बालों और रोमों को नोचना, दाँतों से काटना भी और आत्मगुप्ता से रगड़ना, उसे होश में लाने के लिए हितकर है।
english: Plucking the head-hair and body-hair, biting with the teeth also, and rubbing with ātmaguptā are beneficial for rousing him.
notes: Plant identification: ātmaguptā = Mucuna pruriens (cowhage) (standard). eva ca is rendered 'also'.

hindi: विविध, तीक्ष्ण और मिश्रित मद्यों को, बहुत से कटु द्रव्यों से युक्त करके, उसके मुँह में बार-बार टपकाना चाहिए।
english: Various sharp liquors, compounded and mixed with plenty of pungent [substances], should be poured repeatedly into his mouth.
notes: saṃmūrcchita is taken in the sense 'mixed, compounded' (sam-√murch 'to thicken, combine'), not 'fainted'. kaṭu is taken as pungent substances. saṃmūrcchita may also mean 'intensified, strengthened' (sam-√murch 'to grow strong'); the translation keeps 'compounded'.

words.gloss: with liquor, sour liquids and kāñjika

hindi: इसी प्रकार महौषध से युक्त मातुलुङ्ग का रस, और इसी प्रकार मद्य, अम्ल और काञ्जिक से युक्त सौवर्चल देना चाहिए।
english: Likewise one should give the juice of mātuluṅga combined with mahauṣadha, and likewise sauvarcala salt mixed with liquor, sour liquids and kāñjika (sour fermented liquid).
notes: madyāmlakāñjikaiḥ may also be read as 'liquor and sour kāñjika' (amla qualifying kāñjika). The phrase continues into unit 50 (hiṅgūṣaṇasamāyuktam). Plant identifications: mātuluṅga = Citrus medica (citron) (standard); mahauṣadha = dry ginger, Zingiber officinale (standard).

hindi: हिङ्गु और ऊषण से युक्त करके, जब तक चेतना न जागे तब तक देना चाहिए। चेतना जाग जाने पर उसका हल्के अन्नों से और
english: combined with hiṅgu and ūṣaṇa, until consciousness is awakened. When his consciousness is awakened, one should attend to him with light foods and
notes: hiṅgūṣaṇasamāyuktaṃ agrees with sauvarcalaṃ of unit 49. The sentence of the second line continues through units 51 and 52 (further instrumentals governed by upācaret). Plant identifications: hiṅgu = asafoetida, Ferula assa-foetida (standard); ūṣaṇa = black pepper, Piper nigrum (probable).

hindi: विस्मित करने वाली बातों से, स्मरण कराने से, सुनने में प्रिय बातों से भी, गीत और वाद्यों के स्पष्ट शब्दों से और विचित्र दृश्यों से,
english: with astonishing things, with reminders, indeed with things pleasant to hear, with clear sounds of songs and musical instruments, and with varied sights,

text_flags.why: possible: paḍu is not a Sanskrit word; paṭu 'clear, sharp' agrees with śabdaiḥ (m. inst. pl.) and gives the same metre (ḍ/ṭ confusion)

notes: Continues the instrumentals of unit 50 (upācaret). paṭubhiḥ is taken with śabdaiḥ 'clear (loud) sounds'.

hindi: स्रंसन और उल्लेखन से, धूमों से, अञ्जनों से, कवलग्रहों से, रक्त निकालने से और इसी प्रकार व्यायाम और उद्घर्षण से (उपचार करे)।
english: with laxative purgation and vomiting (ullekhana), with medicated smokings, collyria and holding of mouthfuls (kavalagraha), with lettings of blood, and also with exercise and rubbing.

text_flags.why: the line has 15 syllables as printed; udgharṣaṇaiḥ (the regular noun 'rubbing') restores the 16-syllable half-verse; udgharṣṇa is not a regular form

notes: Ends the sentence begun in unit 50 (upācaret 'one should attend to him').

words.gloss: from the causes of loss of consciousness

hindi: चेतना जाग जाने पर बुद्धिमान (वैद्य) को उसके अनुबन्ध की चिकित्सा करनी चाहिए, क्योंकि उसके मन की प्रलय के कारणों से रक्षा करनी चाहिए।
english: When he has regained consciousness, the intelligent [physician] should treat the after-effect (anubandha), for his mind must be protected from the causes of loss of consciousness (pralaya).
notes: prabuddhasaṃjñaṃ may be a second object ('should treat the man whose consciousness is awakened, [for] the after-effect') or describe the time; both give the same sense. anubandha: what remains or follows (the lingering disorder). pralaya: dissolution, loss of consciousness; taken as a relapse into loss of consciousness.

words.gloss: of those provided with oleation and sweating

hindi: मूर्च्छाओं और मदों में, स्नेहन और स्वेदन किए हुए रोगियों के लिए दोष के अनुसार और बल के अनुसार पाँच कर्म करने चाहिए।
english: In mūrcchāyas and madas, for those who have received oleation and sweating, one should perform the five procedures according to the doṣa and according to strength.
notes: The genitive snehasvedopapannānām is taken as 'for (on) those who have been oleated and sweated'. pañca karmāṇi = the five procedures (pañcakarma).
lines_deva: पञ्च कर्माणि कुर्वीत मूर्च्छायेषु मदेषु च
lines_iast: pañca karmāṇi kurvīta mūrcchāyeṣu madeṣu ca

hindi: अट्ठाईस औषधियों वाले (योग) का, इसी प्रकार तिक्त घृत का, अथवा इसी प्रकार महान् षट्पल (घृत) का प्रयोग प्रशस्त है।
english: The administration of the twenty-eight-drug [preparation], likewise of the bitter ghee, or likewise of the great Ṣaṭpala (six-pala) [ghee], is praised.
notes: These are named preparations whose recipes are not given in this chunk. aṣṭāviṃśatyauṣadhasya may agree with sarpiṣaḥ ('the twenty-eight-drug ghee') as tiktasya does. pala is a measure (value not given here).

hindi: अथवा घी, मधु और शर्करा के साथ त्रिफला का प्रयोग, अथवा शिलाजतु का प्रयोग, अथवा दूध का प्रयोग भी,
english: or the administration of triphalā with ghee, honey (kṣaudra) and sugar, or the administration of śilājatu, or also the administration of milk,
notes: śilājatu kept as the Sanskrit name. The verb praśasyate of unit 57 (and śasyate of unit 55) is understood.

hindi: अथवा दूध के साथ पिप्पलियों का या चित्रक का प्रयोग, रसायनों का अथवा कौम्भ घृत का प्रयोग प्रशस्त है।
english: or the administration of pippalīs or of citraka with milk; the administration of rejuvenatives (rasāyana) or of kaumbha ghee is praised.
notes: payasā 'with milk' may go with both pippalī and citraka. kaumbha: 'of the pitcher (kumbha)', i.e. ghee kept in a pitcher; its age is not stated here. Plant identifications: pippalī = Piper longum (standard); citraka = Plumbago zeylanica (standard).
lines_deva: पिप्पलीनां प्रयोगो वा पयसा चित्रकस्य वा
lines_iast: pippalīnāṃ prayogo vā payasā citrakasya vā

hindi: रक्त निकालने से, और शास्त्रों, सज्जनों तथा सत्त्ववान् लोगों के भी सेवन से देहधारियों के मद और मूर्च्छा शान्त होते हैं।
english: By letting of blood, and by attending to the scriptures, the good and also the strong-minded, the mada and mūrcchāya of embodied beings are allayed.
notes: sevana 'resorting to, attending to' governs the genitives śāstrāṇām, satām and sattvavatām. sattvavat: having a strong mind (sattva).

hindi: यहाँ, दो श्लोक: शुद्ध और अशुद्ध रक्त, उसके कारण, रक्त के दोष से उत्पन्न रोग, और उन रोगों में औषध,
english: Here, the two verses: Pure and impure blood, its causes, the diseases born of vitiation of blood, and the medicine for those diseases,
notes: The dashes after ślokau are punctuation and are left out of the word. The summary sentence runs on into unit 60 (sarvam etat prakāśitam).
lines_deva: विशुद्धं चाविशुद्धं च शोणितं तस्य हेतवः
lines_iast: viśuddhaṃ cāviśuddhaṃ ca śoṇitaṃ tasya hetavaḥ

words.gloss: the causes, signs and medicine of intoxication, fainting and saṃnyāsa
words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa with samāhāra dvandva (neuter)
n. nom. sg., ppp. caus. pra-√kāś

hindi: मद, मूर्च्छा और संन्यास के कारण, लक्षण और औषध — यह सब विधिशोणितक अध्याय में प्रकाशित किया गया है।
english: the causes, signs and medicine of mada, mūrcchāya and saṃnyāsa: all this has been set forth in the chapter Vidhiśoṇitaka.
notes: Closes the summary begun in unit 59. The chapter is called Vidhiśoṇitaka here and Vidhiśoṇitīya in the colophon (P1); both are derived forms of the same title and are not split.

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित, चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में विधिशोणितीय नामक चौबीसवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, in the Śloka section (Ślokasthāna), the twenty-fourth chapter named Vidhiśoṇitīya.
notes: Chapter colophon; the Sanskrit has no verb and the translation keeps it verbless.
lines_deva: इत्यग्निवेशकृते तन्त्रे चरकप्रतिसंस्कृते श्लोकस्थाने विधिशोणितीयो नाम चतुर्विंशोऽध्यायः
lines_iast: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte ślokasthāne vidhiśoṇitīyo nāma caturviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ

hindi: योजनाचतुष्क पूर्ण।
english: Completed: the tetrad on planning (yojanā).
notes: Marks the end of a group of four chapters (catuṣka) named after yojanā 'planning, application (of treatment)'. Verbless as printed.
